stories.headline: Broncos Fall 24-14 to 49ers in Week 4; Surtain, Moss Exit with Injuries
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos dropped to 2-2 on the season Sunday with a 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. Quarterback Bo Nix completed 25 of 42 passes for 214 yards, with 14 of those completions going to running backs, drawing criticism for an over-reliance on checkdowns. Denver's offense managed just 296 yards and failed to establish a consistent ground game, running the ball only nine times in the first half.

The game was further marred by significant injury news for Denver's defense. Starting cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) both exited in the first half, leaving second-year corner Jahdae Barron and reserve Kris Abrams-Draine to finish the game as the starting outside corners. The Broncos' defense held San Francisco's prolific offense to 358 yards but surrendered a back-breaking 56-yard tight end screen touchdown to George Kittle late in the fourth quarter.

A controversial officiating call also played a role, as returner Marvin Mims Jr. was ruled to have fumbled a punt return in the third quarter despite appearing to be down by contact on several replays. The 49ers scored a touchdown nine plays later on the ensuing possession, taking a lead they would not relinquish.

The health of Surtain, Denver's best defensive player and the 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year, is the primary concern heading into the bye week. Coach Sean Payton noted that losing two starting cornerbacks in the same half is an extraordinarily rare circumstance. Barron, the oft-questioned first-round pick, performed creditably in the second half, a potential silver lining from a difficult afternoon.

stories.headline: Nuggets Lose Preseason Opener 109-97 to Jazz; Spencer Jones Out with Hamstring Strain
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets opened their preseason schedule with a 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz in Boulder on Sunday, with the game serving largely as an early tune-up ahead of the regular season opener October 22 in Oklahoma City. Nikola Jokic played 15 minutes and registered seven assists with zero turnovers, while Christian Braun showed encouraging signs of explosiveness with a vicious transition dunk in the first half.

The bigger story out of Denver's camp was the injury to forward Spencer Jones, who underwent an MRI revealing a left hamstring strain suffered during Friday's practice. Jones is considered day-to-day but could miss multiple or all five preseason games. The team said it would err on the side of caution to have him ready for the season opener.

Jones is a key piece of Denver's bench rotation after a breakout 2025-26 campaign in which he shot 39.6 percent from three-point range over 64 games. The Nuggets matched Oklahoma City's two-year, $12 million offer sheet in restricted free agency this offseason to retain him. Jamal Murray also sat out the preseason game for personal reasons, though he was present on the bench in street clothes.

Newcomer DeMar DeRozan came off the bench and was greeted with loud applause from the CU student body at the Boulder venue. Cam Johnson launched six three-pointers in the first half, converting two. Coach David Adelman said the priority for Jones is clearing medical benchmarks — one-on-one, three-on-three and five-on-five sessions — before returning to game action.

stories.headline: Rockies to Hold Rare End-of-Season Press Conference Tuesday After Fourth Straight 100-Loss Season
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rockies finished the 2026 Major League Baseball season with a 58-104 record, marking the fourth consecutive season the franchise has lost 100 or more games — a stretch that places them in dubious company in baseball history. With the playoffs underway for the rest of the league, Rockies president Walker Monfort and president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta are scheduled to hold a media availability session at Coors Field on Tuesday, October 6.

The press conference marks a continued shift in transparency for the organization, which was previously known for radio silence following losing seasons. Last November, ownership and the new front office opened up to questions from the media after announcing a front office restructuring, and the team has maintained that openness throughout a difficult 2026 season.

Among the topics expected to be addressed is the team's arbitration situation, with only six players eligible, including catcher Hunter Goodman and outfielder Jake McCarthy. For both players, the Rockies must weigh not only the cost of arbitration awards but whether either is worth pursuing a longer-term extension.

The Rockies' position player core has drawn some measured optimism from analysts heading into the offseason planning process, even as the pitching staff and overall results remain a significant concern. The Tuesday session will be closely watched by fans and media eager to hear a frank assessment of the organization's direction.

stories.headline: Colorado's U.S. Senate Race: Hickenlooper and Baisley Lay Out Positions on Economy, Healthcare, Tariffs
stories.summary:
Democratic U.S. Sen. John Hickenlooper and Republican challenger state Sen. Mark Baisley sat down with the Colorado Sun ahead of the November 3 election to outline their positions on key issues including the economy, healthcare and immigration. Hickenlooper, 74, is seeking his second Senate term after serving as Denver's mayor and Colorado's governor; Baisley, 71, is a Woodland Park Republican first elected to the state Senate in 2022.

On taxes, Hickenlooper said he would make permanent the tax break for tipped employees while reimposing higher federal income tax rates on the nation's top earners. Baisley expressed broad support for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, saying he appreciates the entirety of what was passed. On tariffs, Hickenlooper called them a significant drag on the economy and said they have been especially harmful to ranchers and farmers, while Baisley signaled general support.

Healthcare was another point of sharp contrast. Hickenlooper supports total transparency in healthcare pricing and a public insurance option, while Baisley favors a consumer-funded model using health savings accounts for routine care and limiting insurance to catastrophic events. On Medicaid work requirements included in recent federal legislation, Hickenlooper called them punitive while Baisley said he supports the concept even as he expressed some concern about unintended consequences.

The race is among several competitive federal contests in Colorado this cycle. Hickenlooper unseated Republican Cory Gardner in 2020 and is running in a state where Democrats hold every statewide office, but national political dynamics and the broader environment make the outcome uncertain.

stories.headline: National Democrats Add Colorado's 3rd Congressional District to Top Targets; Trump PAC Responds with $300K in Spending
stories.summary:
Colorado's 3rd Congressional District, held by Republicans since 2011, has emerged as a top-tier competitive race for the 2026 midterms. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added the district to its red-to-blue list Monday, a designation reserved for races it believes have the strongest prospects for a party flip. At the same time, a super PAC tied to President Donald Trump reported spending more than $300,000 in the district to defend incumbent Republican Rep. Jeff Hurd of Grand Junction.

Hurd is seeking his second term against Democrat Dwayne Romero, a former Aspen city councilman and Army veteran. An internal poll released by Romero over the summer showed the race within one percentage point, well within the margin of error. Hurd won his 2024 race against Adam Frisch, also a former Aspen city councilman, by five percentage points.

The DCCC's red-to-blue designation does not guarantee direct spending in the race but gives Romero access to party training, staff support and fundraising resources. Democratic outside groups have not yet made significant independent expenditures in the district, with spending focused on Colorado's 5th and 8th districts. The No Going Back PAC began its spending in the 3rd District in mid-September.

Colorado Democrats say they have a shot at flipping all four Republican-held U.S. House seats in the state this cycle. The 4th District, where Rep. Lauren Boebert is seeking reelection, is the only GOP-held Colorado seat where the Trump-aligned PAC has not deployed funds, though Boebert has received support from the Congressional Freedom Caucus.

stories.headline: Denver Gazette Editorial Board Releases 2026 Ballot Recommendations Ahead of November Election
stories.summary:
The Denver Gazette editorial board has published its recommendations for candidates and ballot measures facing Denver-area voters on November 3, 2026. The endorsements cover races and questions at the local, state and federal levels relevant to metro Denver residents.

The editorial board's picks provide a conservative-leaning perspective on the November ballot and are intended to guide readers through the full slate of choices they will face when ballots arrive this week. Colorado elections officials confirmed that mail ballots will be sent to registered voters in the coming days, opening the formal voting window.

The Gazette's endorsement package is one of the first major editorial board ballot guides released for the 2026 cycle from a Denver metro outlet. It follows a similar endorsement package from the Colorado Springs Gazette focused on that market, which was published earlier in the week.

stories.headline: Pedestrian Killed After Being Struck by Two Vehicles While Crossing I-76 in Brighton
stories.summary:
A 33-year-old man was killed Saturday night after being struck by two eastbound vehicles while crossing Interstate 76 near East Bromley Lane in Brighton. Brighton police responded to the scene at approximately 7:15 p.m. and found the man with fatal injuries; he was pronounced dead at the scene. His identity is being withheld pending positive identification by the Adams County Coroner's Office and notification of next of kin.

Preliminary investigation indicates the man was crossing the highway on foot when he was first struck by one eastbound vehicle and then hit again by a second eastbound vehicle. Both drivers remained at the scene and cooperated with investigators. The circumstances that brought the pedestrian onto the interstate were not immediately disclosed.

Eastbound lanes of I-76 at the Bromley Lane exit were closed for several hours during the crash investigation before reopening shortly after 11 p.m. The investigation remained ongoing as of Sunday morning. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Brighton Police Department tip line at 303-655-8740.

stories.headline: Great American Beer Festival Returns in Revamped Format at Levitt Pavilion, Oct. 10-11
stories.summary:
The Great American Beer Festival is returning to Denver this year in a significantly overhauled format, moving from the Colorado Convention Center to the outdoor Levitt Pavilion at 1380 W. Florida Ave. and condensing from three days to two, October 10 and 11. Ticket prices dropped sharply, from $85-$95 in 2025 to $60 this year, and the event will feature headlining bands to give it more of a music festival atmosphere.

Total attendance will be capped at 15,000 across all sessions — a dramatic reduction from the 60,000 that attended during the festival's pre-pandemic peak. The Boulder-based Brewers Association, which hosts the event, said the changes reflect shifting consumer tastes, declining beer sales industry-wide and lessons learned from years of softening ticket demand. Sessions will run from noon to 4 p.m., a departure from the evening format used in prior years.

Some 207 breweries will pour beer at the festival, roughly half the number from the event's heyday, but organizers note that approximately 75 percent of participating breweries have won medals at GABF or the World Beer Cup. Pour sizes have also increased, from the historic one-ounce taster to up to four ounces per pour. Breweries themselves will staff the booths rather than the large volunteer corps used in previous years.

The move to an outdoor daytime venue creates new dynamics for the Denver bar, brewery and restaurant scene, with attendees likely to spread out into the surrounding neighborhoods after the sessions end. The festival remains one of the premier beer competitions in the country, and its reinvention comes as the craft beer industry broadly grapples with changing consumption patterns.

stories.headline: Denver Business Leaders Fund $2.5 Million 'Best Return on Life' Image Campaign as State's Business Rankings Slip
stories.summary:
A coalition of prominent Denver-area business leaders has launched a $2.5 million public relations campaign called 'Denver. The Best Return on Life,' aimed at countering what they describe as years of reputational and economic decline in the region. The effort comes as Colorado has fallen to 25th in CNBC's annual ranking of top states for business, down from 11th in recent years, and as the Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce has attributed the slide to what it calls poor policy choices.

The Colorado Chamber of Commerce reports that 98 companies have left the state or changed plans to locate here since 2019, including the corporate headquarters of 34 companies, resulting in an estimated 13,000 lost jobs. The image campaign is intended to attract new businesses, workers and visitors by emphasizing quality-of-life factors. Critics, including some in the business community, argue a marketing campaign cannot offset the regulatory and tax environment they say has driven companies away.

The launch of the campaign reflects broader anxiety among the Denver business community about the metro area's economic trajectory and its standing relative to competing Sun Belt and Mountain West cities. Chamber officials and campaign backers have not detailed the specific media placements or markets the campaign will target.

stories.headline: Colorado Ballots to Arrive This Week as November 3 Election Window Opens
stories.summary:
Colorado registered voters will begin receiving their mail ballots this week, officially opening the voting window for the November 3, 2026 general election. The state's all-mail voting system means the vast majority of Colorado voters will cast their ballots by mail or at drop boxes, with in-person voting centers also available in each county.

The November ballot includes a full slate of federal, state and local races, including the U.S. Senate contest between Democratic incumbent John Hickenlooper and Republican challenger Mark Baisley, all four Republican-held U.S. House seats that Democrats are targeting, and numerous statewide ballot measures. Editorial boards from the Denver Gazette and Colorado Springs Gazette have already released their endorsement packages ahead of ballots going out.

Voters who are not yet registered can do so through Election Day in Colorado under the state's same-day registration law. County election offices are encouraging voters to verify their address on file is current to ensure ballots are delivered without delay.

stories.headline: Pueblo Police Seek Public's Help Finding Stolen Bison Sculpture and Trailer
stories.summary:
Pueblo police are asking for the public's help in locating a stolen homemade trailer and a large metal bison sculpture taken from the parking lot of the SpringHill Suites at 170 S. Santa Fe Ave. early Saturday morning. Surveillance video captured a white four-door short-bed pickup truck entering the lot at 3:38 a.m. and leaving a short time later with the trailer attached, according to a Pueblo Police Department news release.

The stolen trailer is described as black with a passenger-side access panel painted red and two pink ladder hooks on the side. A large metal bison sculpture was inside the trailer at the time of the theft. The owners were staying at the hotel when the items were taken.

Anyone with information on the whereabouts of the trailer, the sculpture or the suspect vehicle is asked to contact Pueblo Police. The theft is under active investigation.

stories.headline: Warm, Sunny Denver Weekend Offers Near-Perfect Leaf-Peeping Conditions in High Country
stories.summary:
Denver is experiencing warm, sunny fall weather this weekend, with temperatures reaching the mid-70s and RealFeel readings near 80 degrees in the metro area. Conditions in the high country are described as near-perfect for fall foliage viewing, with cooler overnight temperatures and recent rain having accelerated color change across Colorado's mountain corridors.

The pleasant stretch comes as Western Slope fire restrictions are being lifted following recent cooler temperatures and rainfall, reducing wildfire risk heading into the late-season period. Outdoor recreation areas near Denver, including mountain passes and popular leaf-peeping drives, are expected to see heavy visitor traffic through the weekend.

Forecasters note that the warm pattern is expected to continue into early next week before seasonal cooling returns to the Front Range.

weather.notable: About 21 degrees above the average high for this time of year!

topStory.headline: Brazil's Presidential Race Heads to October Runoff After Bolsonaro Edges Lula in First Round
topStory.summary:
Brazil's presidential election will proceed to a second round on October 25 after neither candidate secured the outright majority required to win outright. With 99.9 percent of votes counted, far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro received approximately 47 percent of valid votes to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45 percent, translating to roughly 56 million votes for Bolsonaro against 53.8 million for Lula.

The result came as a surprise to pollsters, who had predicted Lula would lead after the first round. Bolsonaro, 45, the eldest son of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro, declared the outcome signaled 'the end of an era' for Lula's Workers' Party, while Lula acknowledged the night was difficult, telling supporters in São Paulo: 'I confess to you that I was convinced I was going to win the election in the first round.' Lula pledged to launch a renewed campaign ahead of the runoff, saying the two-candidate format would allow voters to clearly see the differences between the two men.

The broader Bolsonarista movement performed strongly across Brazil's legislative and gubernatorial races. Jair Bolsonaro's second son Carlos and wife Michelle both won senate seats, his youngest son Jair Renan was elected to the lower house, and former infrastructure minister Tarcísio de Freitas was reelected governor of São Paulo. Of 54 senators elected, 34 were aligned with the right or far right, underscoring the breadth of the movement's gains.

Analysts attributed part of Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected first-round showing to so-called protest votes — supporters of other right-leaning candidates who prioritized defeating Lula and shifted their backing earlier than anticipated. Other first-round candidates, including Ronaldo Caiado with 2.1 percent and Renan Santos with 2.2 percent, have said they will not formally endorse either candidate in the runoff, leaving millions of votes in play. Polls ahead of election day showed the runoff essentially tied.

The stakes extend well beyond Brazil's borders. Latin America's largest economy is grappling with cost-of-living pressures, elevated crime rates, and a strained relationship with the United States, and the region as a whole has trended sharply rightward in recent elections. Jair Bolsonaro, serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup after losing the 2022 election, has endorsed his son's campaign and has expressed hope that a Flávio Bolsonaro victory could lead to his release. The winner of the October 25 runoff will assume office on January 5, 2027.
